attachments.document_title: Notice of termination (letter, message or other record of the notice and its receipt)
attachments.label: A1
attachments.text:
Sonnbühl Management Ltd
Schwyz

Schwyz, 5 June 2026

Termination of employment

We hereby give notice to terminate your employment with Sonnbühl Management Ltd. Your employment will end on 31 August 2026.

Please return your keys and company phone on your last working day. Your final salary statement and your reference will be sent to you after that date.

Kind regards

Tom Tanner
Operations Manager
Sonnbühl Management Ltd

Received on 6 June 2026
Signature: O. Vogel

attachments.document_title: Employment contract or other record of the start of employment
attachments.label: A2
attachments.text:
EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT

between Sonnbühl Management Ltd, Schwyz (employer), represented by Tom Tanner, Operations Manager,
and Owen Vogel, Wiesenstrasse 27, Schwyz (employee)

1. Start of employment: 2 April 2026, for an unlimited period.

2. Position: building services coordinator, part-time (50%).

3. Salary: CHF 1,670 gross per month.

4. Termination: either party may terminate the employment with two months' notice to the end of a calendar month. Notice must be given in writing.

Schwyz, 20 March 2026

The employer: T. Tanner
The employee: O. Vogel

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Was the employee performing Swiss compulsory military service, civil defence service or alternative civilian service on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running, or, for such a service lasting more than eleven days, did either of those fall within the four weeks before or after it?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Was the employee, through no fault of their own, wholly or partly prevented from working by illness or accident on the day notice was given or at some time while the notice period was running, and was the incapacity at that point still within its protected length: up to 30 days in the first year of service, 90 days in the second to fifth years, 180 days from the sixth year?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Where a protected period (illness or accident, compulsory service, pregnancy or birth, as above) is raised: was the notice given before that period began, with the notice period not yet expired when it began?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Was the notice given while the probation period was still running, counting any extension of the probation period under art. 335b para. 3 (a probation period interrupted by illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation is extended accordingly)?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Was the employee pregnant, or within sixteen weeks after giving birth, on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual agreement, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract set a probation period other than the first month of employment?

text:
Hi,

Sonnbühl Management Ltd in Schwyz has let me go. Tom Tanner, the operations manager, gave me the letter on 5 June 2026 and I signed for it the next morning. I'd only been there since the beginning of April.

My contract is attached as well. Please look at the part about notice, because that's where Mr Tanner and I don't agree. My written contract says two months' notice to the end of a month. I know that in the first year the normal rule is just one month, but my contract sets two, and I signed it that way on purpose because I gave up a secure job to move here.

Mr Tanner's letter, which I've also attached, has me finishing at the end of August. He says that's generous. But he has also told me my last pay will only cover June and July, because 'in the first year it's one month anyway', and he wants me to use up my holidays in August. I earn CHF 1,670 a month for my part-time post, so for me it's a lot of money.

One more thing, since a friend asked me whether pregnancy rules might help: no, that doesn't apply to me at all. I'm a man, I wasn't pregnant and I haven't had a baby.

I'd like to know who is right about the notice and how much they should actually pay me.

Thanks,
Owen Vogel
Wiesenstrasse 27, Schwyz
